sentences.text: On search of the vehicle, bottles of mis- branded and adulterated cold drinks were recovered.
The matter was investigated and on completion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed against the applicant and three others under Sections 420, 272, 273 of IPC.
On receipt of charge-sheet, learned Magistrate took cognizance in the matter and the matter was committed to the court of Sessions.
By the order of Special Judicial Magistrate 1st, the sample of alleged adulterated soft drink was soft for examination before Forensic Science Laboratory.
However, examination was not done by the Laboratory as the facility of examining adulterated cold-drinks was not available there.
Thereafter, the said samples were sent for chemical examination before the Public Analyst U.P. Lucknow.
As per report of Public Analyst, the alleged sample was found to be adulterated.
Thereafter, the matter was fixed for hearing on framing of charges.

After hearing the respective parties, learned Additional Sessions Judge, Vikasnagar, Dehradun, vide order dated 06.12.2014,
observed that there are no sufficient ground for discharge of the applicant from the said offences and fixed the date as 23.12.2014 for framing of charge.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire material brought on record.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the sample was not found noxious as such offence under Sections 272, 273 of IPC is not made out against the applicant; at the most offence under The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is made out.

5. Before any discussion, Section 227 of The Code of Criminal Procedure (for short, Cr.P.C.) would be apt to reproduce here, which is as under:-
"227. Discharge.-

If, upon consideration of the record of the case and documents submitted therewith, and after hearing the submissions of the accused and the prosecution in this behalf, the Judge considers that there is not sufficient ground for proceedings against the accused, he shall discharge the accused and record his reasons for so doing."
6.
The law with regard to framing of charge is no more res integra having been settled in catena of decisions.
Under Section 227 of Cr.P.C., the trial court has merely to sift the evidence in order to find out whether or not there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

The sufficiency of ground would take within its fold the nature of the evidence recorded by the police or the documents produced before the court which ex facie disclose that there are suspicious circumstances against the accused so as to frame a charge against him.
7. In view of foregoing discussion, I do not find any illegality, perversity or any jurisdictional error in the order impugned.
Present criminal misc. application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is devoid of merit.
Same is hereby dismissed.
8. Interim order dated 06.12.2016 stands vacated.
(Lok Pal Singh, J.) 13.03.2020
